meeting_header:
Date: 2025-08-22 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 55m
Attendees: Lena Martinez (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SA), Rachel Kim (StrataGrid Partnerships), Tom O'Neal (StrataGrid Infra), Priya Singh (StrataGrid Cloud), Marcus Leung (StrataGrid BD), Victor (StrataGrid Legal - partial)
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and StrataGrid to explore integration options for edge GPU fleet and cloud bursting. Covered technical constraints (MIG, drivers, VPC peering), commercial model fit, and next steps for a technical deep dive and pilot scope. Agreement to share docs, inventory, and schedule an operator-level meeting.
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Martinez: hi everyone, thanks for joining. this is lena from redwood inference, i'll kick off real quick, then samir will go into the infra bits.
[00:06] Rachel Kim: thanks lena, excited to chat. we are exploring partners that can help with cloud + edge gpu orchestration.
[00:12] Samir Patel: hey team, samir here, redwood se. quick note: this call is discovery, so we'll ask about your fleet, networking, and what success looks like.
[00:20] Tom O'Neal: cool. just to set context, strata grid runs a mix of on-prem edge islands and a public cloud pool. our edge nodes are mostly A100s and a handful of L40s. some sites have multi-tenant constraints.
[00:35] Jordan Lee: when you say "edge islands" do you mean isolated networks with NAT and no outbound egress? or are they peered?
[00:41] Tom O'Neal: mostly isolated, some sites have private egress via VPN to our central VPC. others are air-gapped for telco customers.
[00:48] Lena Martinez: ok that matters for our private deploy model and whether we do a control plane in your VPC or full on-prem runtime.
[00:56] Priya Singh: a big ask from customers is consistent inference latency and the ability to burst to cloud, but keep data residency.
[01:03] Samir Patel: understood — redwood supports routing policies for burst to hosted instances or dedicated pools. we have a private control plane option for VPCs; for air-gapped we'll need to talk about an on-prem package.
[01:12] Marcus Leung: commercial question up front — do you do revenue share or is this purely integrations + referral?
[01:18] Lena Martinez: short answer: we have a few partner models, referral/technical partner, and strategic reseller/embedded in dedicated. we can share the partner one-pager.
[01:25] Rachel Kim: great. from a tech standpoint, can you speak to driver and kernel requirements? a lot of our edge boxes run older driver stacks.
[01:33] Samir Patel: sure. redwood runtime prefers CUDA 12.x for some recent kernels but we have fallbacks. two paths — vendor drivers (nvidia) with specific CUDA and cuDNN, or an AMI/container that packages runtime dependencies. the operator can install the correct drivers if you allow kernel module install.
[01:45] Tom O'Neal: ok that might be tricky for telco sites that lock kernel changes. what are fallback options?
[01:49] Samir Patel: fallback is containerized with userspace-only optimizations, or run in a cloud-burst mode where model runs on your cloud pool. we also have quantized model variants that are more forgiving on older drivers.
[02:01] Rachel Kim: you mentioned quantized models — how big is the performance delta?
[02:06] Jordan Lee: depends on model and quant — for 8-bit you typically see 1.1–1.6x slower in some cases but with big memory savings. depends on batch size and sequence length.
[02:18] Tom O'Neal: curious about support for MIG/partitioning on A100s. we sometimes carve GPUs for multi-tenant customers.
[02:24] Samir Patel: we support MIG on Ampere-family but with some caveats around kernel versions and NVML visibility. we'll need to validate on your exact driver level.
[02:33] Lena Martinez: is multi-tenant isolation a hard requirement?
[02:35] Priya Singh: yes for a set of our customers. they expect strong isolation and per-tenant logging.
[02:40] Samir Patel: Redwood's runtime supports per-tenant namespaces, token-level billing and audit logs; but for MIG-level isolation we rely on the hardware + driver. we'll surface gaps if any.
[02:51] Marcus Leung: what about compliance? SOC2, SSO, SAML, KMS?
[02:55] Lena Martinez: good point — we are SOC 2 compliant. we support SSO via SAML/Okta, RBAC, and integrations with KMS/HSM for Private deployments. for Hosted the keys are managed by Redwood but enterprise customers can bring their own KMS.
[03:09] Rachel Kim: that helps. can you also sign an NDA? our legal would want that before detailed configs.
[03:14] Lena Martinez: yes we can. i'll start the NDA thread after the call.
[03:17] [03:17] Victor (strata legal): brief hello — i'll review nda and licensing.
[03:20] Tom O'Neal: shifting to the operational model: how do you handle OS updates and driver rollouts? we need a maintenance window plan.
[03:28] Samir Patel: we recommend a canary rollout through your k8s cluster with automatic fallback; Redwood Console supports model rollouts and traffic slices, but OS kernel updates are owned by the infra team — we provide recommended playbook and scripts.
[03:40] Rachel Kim: what's the pilot scoping look like? quick POC or multi-site pilot?
[03:45] Lena Martinez: usually a 6–8 week pilot: week 1–2 prep & install, week 3–4 run benchmarks and telemetry collection, week 5–6 iterate and test failover patterns. can be shortened if the site is cloud-ready.
[03:59] Tom O'Neal: benchmarks — do you have a standard harness? we prefer to run our own load generator.
[04:04] Samir Patel: we can share our benchmark repo and also run side-by-side runs. common pattern: you run your generator and we provide a client harness to measure tail latency, p50/p95, throughput and token cost.
[04:15] Priya Singh: latency SLOs matter — what tail latencies can you hit on a single A100 for 8k context models?
[04:22] Jordan Lee: roughly p95 in 60–150ms per token depending on model and batch sizes; that's from our verified profiles but we should validate on your workload.
[04:31] Rachel Kim: any known incompatible models or architectures?
[04:34] Samir Patel: some experimental models with custom ops require extra kernel builds; upstream LLMs generally fine.
[04:39] Marcus Leung: how do we surface joint GTM? any revenue share?
[04:44] Lena Martinez: business dev will draft a partner agreement with referral credits and co-sell options. specifics TBD after pilot success metrics.
[04:51] Tom O'Neal: technical question — do you support Kubernetes operator or a binary runtime?
[04:55] Samir Patel: both — we have a K8s operator for the private runtime that manages pods, drivers, and model mounts; plus a lightweight binary for single-node edge deployments.
[05:05] Rachel Kim: great. can you clarify network requirements for the control plane? some of our edge nodes can't reach internet at all.
[05:11] Samir Patel: for fully air-gapped sites we provide an on-prem bundle that includes control-plane components with offline license tokens; for partially-connected sites we can do a VPC peering or VPN to the control plane.
[05:21] Tom O'Neal: do you have size constraints for the on-prem package? our smallest box is an L40 with 48GB VRAM.
[05:27] Jordan Lee: that's fine; our binary supports L40 class. we will need to tune batch sizes and kv-cache settings.
[05:33] Rachel Kim: ok, change of topic: what about model updates and provenance? customers want reproducible model versions and rollback.
[05:40] Lena Martinez: Redwood has model versioning and rollout controls; you can pin model versions per customer and we keep rollout audit logs.
[05:46] Priya Singh: are there telemetry data retention controls?
[05:49] Samir Patel: yes, retention is configurable and we can integrate with your SIEM.
[05:53] Marcus Leung: any preference on what Redwood expects from partners during pilot (SLA, monitoring)?
[05:58] Lena Martinez: partners typically provide node access, inventory, and a single point of contact. Redwood will provide installer scripts, monitoring dashboards, and a runbook for incident handoff.
[06:08] Rachel Kim: let's talk timelines — we'd like to go to pilot by late september. feasible?
[06:12] Lena Martinez: yes that's reasonable. we'll align resources after NDA.
[06:15] Tom O'Neal: one more: hardware telemetry agent — do you require a collector?
[06:18] Samir Patel: we can accept existing collectors (prometheus metrics) or deploy a Redwood sidecar exporter.
[06:24] [06:24] Rachel Kim: ok folks, this has been super helpful. next steps?
[06:27] Lena Martinez: i'll recap: lena sends NDA and partner one-pager; samir will share tech note and helm references; tom will send current inventory and driver versions; schedule operator deep dive for next week.
[06:39] Victor (legal): i'll coordinate NDA review windows, expect a 48–72 hour turnaround.
[06:44] Lena Martinez: great — any final Qs?
[06:46] Marcus Leung: just one on price: is there a trial credit or dev environment?
[06:50] Lena Martinez: we typically provide dev credits for pilot customers and can discuss commercial terms in parallel.
[06:55] Rachel Kim: thanks everyone. talk soon.
[06:58] [END]
